Clean data¶

There are a lot of problems with this data 🤦‍♂️¶

  • "!" where there should be numbers
  • "NaN"
  • A period during which the operating conditions changed
  • A period where a flow rate was abnormally low
  • two temperature sensors were alternatingly switched on and off
  • the impurity sampling was sparse and was linearly interpolated to match x sampling

Filter out from 8/22/2016 to 12/16/2016¶

Process operation knowledge conﬁrmed that the operating conditions from 8/22/2016 to 12/16/2016 was changed due to a business decision that will not recur in subsequent operations. Therefore, this period of data will not be used for model training.

3.3. Detecting interpolated impurity data points¶

In [70]:

                         y= dff['y:Impurity'],

In [ ]:
def remove_interpolated_points(t_datetime, y, slope_tol=1e-5):
    """
    Remove linearly interpolated points by detecting constant-slope segments.
    
    
    """
    t_datetime = pd.to_datetime(t_datetime)
    t_numeric = (t_datetime - t_datetime.iloc[0]).dt.total_seconds().values
    y = np.asarray(y, dtype=float)
    
    if len(y) <= 2:
        return t_datetime.values, y
    
    slopes = np.diff(y) / np.diff(t_numeric)
    
    slope_changes = np.abs(np.diff(slopes))
    
    keep = np.ones(len(y), dtype=bool)
    for i in range(len(slope_changes)):
        if slope_changes[i] <= slope_tol:
            keep[i + 1] = False  
    
    return t_datetime.values[keep], y[keep], keep
In [72]:
t_datetime = dff['Date']

import re

df_f2 = dff[lin_mask].copy().reset_index(drop=True)

x_cols = [col for col in df_f2.columns if col.startswith('x')]

def x_sort_key(c):
    match = re.match(r'^x(\d+):', c)
    if match:
        return (0, int(match.group(1)), c)
    return (1, c)

x_cols = sorted(x_cols, key=x_sort_key)

X = df_f2[x_cols].values
Y = df_f2['y:Impurity'].values

X_scaled = scaler.fit_transform(X)

In [ ]:
import re


def sort_key(c):
    if c.startswith('x'):
        
        return (0, int(re.match(r'x(\d+)', c).group(1)))
    if c.startswith('Avg'):
        
        return (1, c)
    if c.startswith('y'):
        
        return (2, c)
    
    return (3, c)


d = df_f2.loc[:,'x10:Primary Column Bed1 DP':'y:Impurity']
d = d[sorted(d.columns, key=sort_key)]

Correlation Plot¶

In [76]:
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
sns.heatmap(d.corr(), cmap='RdBu_r', vmin=-1, vmax=1, fmt='.2f',
           xticklabels=[c[:3] for c in d.columns],
           yticklabels=[c[:3] for c in d.columns], )
plt.tick_params(labelsize=8)
title('Feature Correlaton')
plt.show()

Qin et al. have similar results, but my results still struggle with missing some interpolated points. Most notably, Qin et al deleted many "outlier" points when they showed unusual values for the subplots for each sensor (x1, etc.). I think that this is a mistake, as it can be seen that some of these peaks are actually plateaus, lasting for 6 hours or so. This seems like it is more likely a deliberate attempt to modify an aspect of the reactor, and observe if it produces a change in the impurity concentration.
